children: said on Friday the U.S. Export-Import Bank had issued a letter of interest indicating it may provide up to $750 million in financing for the miner's planned rare-earth separation, metals and alloys facility in Louisiana.
The development comes as the U.S. seeks to strengthen domestic critical minerals supply chains and reduce its reliance on China for rare-earth processing.
Potential financing could cover up to $750 million of project costs with a repayment tenor of up to 15 years under EXIM's Make More in America initiative, Aclara said.
Project Dynamo is planned to include rare-earth separation, metals and alloys production capabilities at the Port of Vinton, Louisiana.
The company said the facility will process rare-earth materials from its South American assets into individual rare-earth oxides, including neodymium-praseodymium, dysprosium and terbium.
Aclara is seeking to build an integrated mine-to-alloy rare-earth supply chain serving industries including electric vehicles, robotics, advanced technologies, power generation and AI infrastructure.

The company said the Louisiana facility is expected to be construction-ready by the end of 2026, adding that EXIM's interest remains subject to approvals and does not represent a final financing commitment.
